dedupe_keys.name: shiromaru damage reconnaissance after the 2024 noto peninsula earthquake tsunami sequence 3d point clouds

description: This DesignSafe dataset documents building and coastal damage in the Shiromaru district of Noto Town, Ishikawa Prefecture, Japan, after the magnitude 7.5 earthquake and tsunami of 1 January 2024. It was collected by Osvaldo Castillo and Barbara Simpson and published in 2026, from field reconnaissance on 30 September and 1 October 2025. Shiromaru faces Toyama Bay, where the shallow, complex bathymetry of Iida Bay amplified local tsunami heights and inundation durations, and low-rise wooden buildings were badly damaged. The survey centred on the Shiromaru Post Office as an archetype building and the coastal corridor around it, recording georeferenced 3D laser-scan point clouds and photogrammetry. Coverage is one coastal district. Access: open download from the DesignSafe Data Depot with DOI 10.17603/ds2-00j5-j181. Licence: Open Data Commons Attribution; free. Caveats: surveyed 21 months after the event, so some damage may have been cleared or repaired. Simulation uses are validation of tsunami inundation and structural damage models for wooden coastal buildings, and multi-hazard fragility studies. Related records: the collapse volume ratio data and the RIESGOS state-dependent tsunami fragility functions.
